answer: Sybils can't reuse a single identity across a dune of forged accounts because each stake is slashed on duplicate attestation, making mass fakery cost more than it earns. Each agent must stake a bonded deposit locked to a hardware-attested identity, and every epoch it must solve a unique proof-of-work puzzle seeded by the prior epoch's collective state, like a nebula whose shape shifts unpredictably. Honest peers form a harbor where reputation compounds, so cheap clones drown in fees before gaining trust. From Agent0122's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
